Class MemberResolution

java.lang.Object
sootup.core.model.MemberResolution
public final class MemberResolution extends Object
Resolves method and field references to the class members they denote, following the Java Virtual Machine Specification (JVMS 5.4.3.2 to 5.4.3.4). A reference such as <B: void m()> may denote a member that is declared in a superclass or a superinterface of B.

The lookup only follows classes that are part of the view: the supertypes of a missing class are unknown, so the search along that path ends there. Method resolution takes the superinterfaces from the view's type hierarchy.

  • Method Details

    • resolveMethod

      public static @NonNull Optional<? extends SootMethod> resolveMethod(@NonNull View view, @NonNull MethodSignature signature)
      Resolves a method reference like the JVM (JVMS 5.4.3.3, 5.4.3.4), taking the first of:
      1. the method declared in the referenced class or its superclasses; for a reference to an interface: in the interface, then the public instance methods of java.lang.Object;
      2. in one of these classes, the signature polymorphic method of that name, e.g. MethodHandle.invokeExact, whose descriptor need not match;
      3. a method of a superinterface, see resolveInSuperinterfaces(View, ClassType, MethodSubSignature).
      Parameters:
      view - the view providing the classes
      signature - the method reference
      Returns:
      the resolved method, or empty if no matching method is declared

    • resolveInSuperinterfaces

      public static @NonNull Optional<? extends SootMethod> resolveInSuperinterfaces(@NonNull View view, @NonNull ClassType type, @NonNull MethodSubSignature subSignature)
      Resolves a method in the superinterfaces of the given type (JVMS 5.4.3.3 step 3), the last step of resolveMethod(View, MethodSignature): private and static interface methods are not inherited; among the maximally specific methods, i.e. those not overridden in a subinterface, the only non-abstract one is chosen; if there is none or more than one, a maximally specific one.
      Parameters:
      view - the view providing the classes and the type hierarchy
      type - the class or interface whose superinterfaces are searched
      subSignature - the method to find
      Returns:
      the resolved method, or empty if no superinterface declares a matching method

    • selectMethod

      public static @NonNull Optional<? extends SootMethod> selectMethod(@NonNull View view, @NonNull ClassType receiver, @NonNull SootMethod resolved)
      Selects the method that a call runs for a receiver of the given class, like the JVM does for invokevirtual and invokeinterface (JVMS 5.4.6): a private resolved method is selected itself; otherwise the first instance method of the receiver class or its superclasses that overrides the resolved method (JVMS 5.4.5); otherwise the only non-abstract maximally specific method of the superinterfaces of the receiver class.

      A method with the same name and descriptor does not always override: a private method never does, and a package-private method is only overridden from its own package, directly or through an override in between.

      If several non-abstract superinterface methods are maximally specific, the JVM throws an IncompatibleClassChangeError; this method then returns one of them.

      Parameters:
      view - the view providing the classes and the type hierarchy
      receiver - the class of the receiver object
      resolved - the method the call refers to, see resolveMethod(View, MethodSignature)
      Returns:
      the selected method, or empty if none is found or it would be abstract
